sentences.text: The only known material of Jian consists of an articulated pectoral girdle together with portions of the forelimb, including the humerus, radius, and ulna.
It is interpreted as a medium-sized member of the microraptorine group, larger than the diminutive Microraptor and Zhongjianosaurus but smaller than Sinornithosaurus and Changyuraptor.
The scapula and coracoid are firmly fused, indicating that the specimen represents a skeletally mature individual.

Among its distinguishing traits are an unusually high coracoid-to-humerus proportion, distal humeral condyles that lie mainly on the front side, and a conspicuous foramen at the apex of the radius when viewed from below.
Jian changmaensis is the first non-avian dinosaur formally described from the Xiagou Formation, which had previously yielded more than a hundred bird fossils.
At the same locality, researchers have uncovered piles of shattered bird bones that resemble the regurgitated pellets of modern owls.
The fossils were uncovered in 2008 within the Xiagou Formation near the village of Changma in north-west Gansu Province, China.
Ling-Qi Zhou and colleagues formally named the new genus and species in 2026, designating specimen GSGM-D050 as the holotype, the reference specimen for the taxon.
The holotype is curated permanently at the Gansu Geological Museum under the accession number GSGM-D050.
The material was first mentioned in a conference abstract released in 2010.

Because Jian is the only non-bird predator present at the site and one of the larger microraptorines, researchers propose that it may have been responsible for the accumulation of the broken bird remains.
Jian belongs to the dromaeosaurid family, specifically within the microraptorine subfamily.
Within that subfamily it falls into an unresolved polytomy alongside Hesperonychus, Microraptor, and Zhongjianosaurus.
Jian lived during the Early Cretaceous Aptian age.
Its age is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Current phylogenetic studies have not resolved the precise position of Jian within Microraptorinae.
